mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a decline in demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of reduced economic activity and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 10% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the months where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in a month signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both RSAFS increased and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure during a period of high interest rates, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
regime_hint: inflationary period with high interest rates
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to grow.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 2%.
